papers.title: The spectrum of units of algebraic $K$-theory
papers.abstract: It is well known that the $[0,1]$ and $[0,2]$ Postnikov truncations of the units of the topological $K$-theories $\glone \KO$ and $\glone \KU$, respectively, are split, and that the splitting is provided by the ($\Z/2$-graded) line bundles. In this paper we give a similar splitting for the $[0,1]$-truncation of the units of algebraic $K$-theory, considered as a sheaf on affine schemes. A crucial step is to produce the splitting for $\glone K(\Z)$. Along the way we also give a complete calculation of the connective spectrum of strict units of $K(\Z)$ and $K(\F_\ell)$ for a prime $\ell$. Finally, we show that the units of algebraic $K$-theory do not split as a presheaf. In fact we show they do not even split pointwise.

papers.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
papers.abstract:
We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd,
  \qquad
  \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[
  \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!,
  \qquad
  \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.

papers.title: Equivariant $K$-theory as a global localization
papers.abstract: We establish a global equivariant refinement of the theorem of Snaith that presents the complex $K$-theory spectrum as a localization of the suspension spectrum of $\mathbb C P^\infty$. We prove that the morphism of ultra-commutative global ring spectra from $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$ that classifies the tautological $U(1)$-representation exhibits the global $K$-theory spectrum as a specific localization, in both the $\infty$-categories of ultra-commutative ring spectra and of commutative global ring spectra. The classes to be inverted are certain representation-graded $U(n)$-equivariant homotopy classes of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\text{gl}} U(1)$, the pre-Bott classes. We also show that for every compact Lie group $G$, the $G$-equivariant $K$-theory spectrum is a telescopic localization of $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_G U(1)$ by the pre-Bott classes of all unitary $G$-representations.

papers.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.

papers.title: Nilpotent Deformation Theory via Ultrasolid Algebra
papers.abstract: Deformation theory studies how varieties and other algebro-geometric objects vary in families. A central part of the subject is formal deformation theory, where one deforms over an Artinian base; such deformation problems are governed by Lie algebraic models. We pose the question of deforming varieties over nilpotent but not necessarily Artinian bases. These turn out to be classified by the same Lie algebraic models plus some topological structure. More precisely, we will consider partition Lie algebroids in the category of ultrasolid modules, a variation of the solid modules of Clausen and Scholze that give a well-behaved category akin to topological modules. To approach this result, we decompose deformation problems into n-nilpotent layers. Each of these layers is individually easier to understand, and is classified by simpler variants of partition Lie algebras.

papers.title: Normed idempotence of spectra and distributivity in equivariant higher algebra
papers.abstract: We introduce and develop the theory of distributivity for base categories equipped with so-called atomic orbital subcategories, with an eye towards applications in equivariant homotopy theory. This extends the important framework in Nardin's thesis and supplies several crucial details on distributivity missing from the treatment therein. As our main technical result, we provide a parametrised distributive version of the universal property of "partial cocompletions with relations". We then employ this to construct a distributively normed symmetric monoidal structure on presentable categories. In turn, by specialising to the case of equivariant homotopy theory for compact Lie groups G, we show that the category of genuine G-spectra is normed idempotent, so that we obtain the structure of multiplicative norms on G-spectra along inclusions of finite index subgroups.

papers.title: The invariant cell number property for $\mathbb{E}_4$-rings
papers.abstract: For any non-zero $\mathbb{E}_4$-ring $R$, we prove that an $n$-fold direct sum of suspensions of $R$ cannot admit an exhaustive filtration by fewer than $n$ cells. We do this by showing that certain integral representations of the symmetric group lift to Schur functors on additively $\mathbb{E}_3$-monoidal $\infty$-categories. We then reduce the statement to a vanishing fact for rational Schur functors due to Deligne.

papers.title: Unbounded Nilpotency Gaps on Rationally Elliptic Manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct simply connected, closed smooth manifolds whose rational homotopy types are elliptic and whose homology nilpotency exceeds rational category by arbitrarily large amounts. This separates short models from short quotients of minimal models. The construction starts from an explicit family of minimal Sullivan algebras with finite-dimensional cohomology. A finite quotient establishes Poincar\'e duality and gives an upper bound for homology nilpotency, while a closed orientation functional computes rational category. Two forced primitives yield the lower bound. An even regrading separates the relevant weights, extending this obstruction to every graded acyclic differential ideal. Rational surgery realizes the resulting models in their formal dimensions, with vanishing rational Pontryagin classes and arbitrarily large rational connectivity. The ratio of homology nilpotency to rational category tends to four thirds. Finally, under an external spherical stabilization statement, attaching a single cone can increase homology nilpotency by an arbitrarily large amount while leaving rational category unchanged.

papers.title: The real Betti realization of very effective Hermitian K-theory
papers.abstract: Real Betti realization is a symmetric monoidal functor from the category of motivic spectra to that of topological spectra, extending the functor that associates to a scheme over $\mathbb{R}$ the space of its real points. In this article, we identify the $\mathcal{E}_1$-ring structure on the real realization of $\mathsf{ko}$, the very effective cover of Hermitian K-theory $\mathsf{KO}$, by an explicit 2-local fracture square, as being equivalent to $\mathsf{L}(\mathbb{R})_{\geq 0}$, the connective L-theory spectrum of $\mathbb{R}$. Along the way, we also compute the real realization of other motivic ring spectra: motivic cohomology $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}/2$, the variant $\widetilde{\mathsf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$, $\mathsf{KO}$, the very effective cover $\mathsf{kgl}$ of algebraic K-theory $\mathsf{KGL}$.

papers.title: A counterexample to a conjecture of Plotnick on knot exteriors
papers.abstract: We resolve a conjecture of S. Plotnick from 1983 concerning the homotopy type of four-dimensional knot complements. We show that the exteriors of two branched twist spins of the trefoil, which were shown by Plotnick not to be homotopy equivalent as boundary pairs and hence not homeomorphic, are in fact simple homotopy equivalent. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of an explicit element of augmentation $49$ in the integral group ring of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5)$ which is a unit modulo the group norm and commutes with the element inducing the monodromy on the fundamental group.

papers.title: Global transfer systems and endopurity of subgroups
papers.abstract: Global transfer systems are combinatorial objects that parametrize intermediate levels of structures and properties in globally equivariant homotopy theory. In this paper we study the lattice of global transfer systems, expanding beyond the case of abelian groups which was computed by the second author. The main result is a proof that the irreducible elements of the lattice of global transfer systems are strictly controlled by subgroups of groups which we refer to as endopure. From the irreducible elements one can recover the whole lattice, and studying these endopure subgroups leads us to a wide range of new phenomena and computations.

papers.title: Integral homology lattices of matching and circulant complexes
papers.abstract: Bouc's hook cycles span the rational top homology of the matching complex of $K_{2k+1}$. We prove that their integral saturation quotient has exponent exactly $2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$ for every $k\geq1$, and construct divided-power cycles attaining this bound. For $k\geq2$, the homology lattice is not isomorphic to the standard integral hook lattice as an $\mathfrak S_{2k+1}$-module. For circulant complexes, we determine the integral dihedral homology modules of $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s}^{s-1})$, $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+1}^{s-1})$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+2}^{s-1})$, for $s\geq3$, $s\geq2$ and $s\geq3$, respectively, and classify the least scalar lifts of all primitive equivariant quotients to the rank-one module with trivial rotation and negative reflection. Tate localization relates prime-order gluing to fixed-point homology under a free, single-degree homology hypothesis. Explicit cycle subgroups separate saturation defects from obstructions to equivariant sections. For circulant independence complexes with jumps two and three, we prove an eight-periodic ordinary homotopy classification and a fixed-space obstruction to uniform representation suspensions. For every fixed nonempty bounded positive jump set, a finite-state construction gives a rational critical-face series.

papers.title: Non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery
papers.abstract: We give homotopy-theoretic proofs of the principal results of non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery. These include the Fundamental Theorem of Poincar\'e surgery, the Poincar\'e transversality exact sequence, and the construction of Poincar\'e handle structures. All results apply in dimensions~$\ge 8$.

papers.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.

papers.title: Resolutions of orbifold generalised triangle groups
papers.abstract: Let $T=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}=1\rangle$ be a generalised triangle group in which $W$ is the Farey word of a rational slope $q=r/s$, and suppose that $T$ is the fundamental group of a hyperbolic $3$-orbifold whose singular locus has no spherical vertices. Let $G=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}\rangle$ be the associated central extension. We compute an explicit free resolution of the trivial module over $\mathbb{Z}G$ of minimal length, with differentials given in closed form by Fox derivatives. From this resolution we deduce an explicit free resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ which is $2$-periodic in degrees at least two, and we compute the integral homology and cohomology of both groups. Strebel treated the classical family $q=0/1$ in 1983. Since then only the family $q=1/2$ has been treated, by Ellis and Williams, and for that family our resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ has strictly smaller rank in every degree.

papers.title: A $p$-adic Riemann--Hilbert correspondence over Robba rings
papers.abstract: We construct overconvergent period sheaves $\mathcal{O}\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^{I,\dagger}$ and $\mathcal{O}\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{\dagger,+}$ on the $v$-site of a liftable semi-stable formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}_Z$. By establishing a decompletion theorem for small representations, we prove a $p$-adic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence relating small $\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^I$-local systems (resp. $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-local systems) on the generic fiber $X_Z$ to small flat connections on the associated period ringed spaces. We further analyze the local Frobenius action and show that this correspondence is compatible with the Frobenius structure. As an application, we prove a comparison theorem between the cohomology of these period sheaves and the rigid cohomology of the special fiber, refining results of Le Bras and Colmez--Nizio{\l}.

papers.title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Delta_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\Delta_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

papers.title: A finite-delay code for lexicographic graph products
papers.abstract: For all finite simple graphs, the strong product and both ordered lexicographic products have the same Shannon capacity, answering a question of Sason. An explicit code conversion delays one component by a single block, with rate loss tending to zero. The equality extends to arbitrary mixtures of the two products and survives adjoining an additional strong-product factor.

papers.title: A GLSM realization of derived equivalence in $U(1) \times U(2)$ models
papers.abstract: This paper studies the derived equivalence between Calabi--Yau mixed branches using the B-brane hemisphere partition function in anomalous gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs). For a family of anomalous $U(2)$ GLSMs, we study the infrared behavior of B-branes under RG flow and the variation of FI parameters in the quantum K\"ahler moduli space. As characterized by the big and small window categories of the GLSM, the RG flow effect is analyzed according to the properties of their B-brane central charges as hemisphere partition functions. The result generalizes the band restriction rules in anomalous abelian GLSMs (Clingempeel--Floch--Romo) to some $U(2)$ models. As an application, we study a family of $U(1)\times U(k)$ models for $k=1,2$, which realize a Fano UV sigma model and two IR phases as mixed branches accompanied by local Calabi--Yau Higgs components. By applying the restriction rules, we establish new derived equivalences between Calabi--Yau varieties from these anomalous models.

papers.title: A Krause-type recollement for Q-shaped derived categories
papers.abstract: Let k be a commutative noetherian hereditary ring and let Q be a small, Hom-finite, locally bounded k-linear category admitting a Serre functor and satisfying the strong retraction property, with nilpotent pseudo-radical. For every k-algebra A, we construct a recollement of the Q-shaped homo?topy category KQ(A Inj) of objectwise injective Q-shaped modules by its full subcategory Kac Q (A Inj) of exact objects and the Q-shaped derived category DQ(A). The construction uses complete hereditary cotorsion pairs and does not require A to be noetherian. If A is left noetherian, both KQ(A Inj) and Kac Q (A Inj) are compactly generated by special preenvelopes of finitely generat?ed stalk modules. We identify (Kac Q (A Inj))c with the idempotent completion of (KQ(A Inj))c/LI ((DQ(A))c ), where LI is the fully faithful left adjoint of the localization. This paper builds on and generalizes works of Krause and Liu

papers.title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
papers.abstract: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Der\'e. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.

papers.title: A Proof of the Jung-Kim Conjecture on the Centers of Walled Brauer Algebras
papers.abstract: We give a unified account of the five families of Khovanov arc algebras $K_n^m$, $K_n^{-\infty}$, $K_n^{+\infty}$, $K_n^\infty$ and $K_\infty^\infty$ in the framework of level-two tensor product categorifications, making explicit a perspective familiar to specialists. Our main application is a proof of the Jung--Kim conjecture: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the centre of every walled Brauer algebra is generated by supersymmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements. We also give a homogeneous basis of the centre in terms of arc diagrams, for the grading induced by $K_\infty^\infty$. The proof combines a calculation of the arc-algebra centre with an explicit comparison of central actions under the Brundan--Stroppel Morita equivalence and Brundan-Kleshchev isomorphism. Along the way, we explain the relation between $K_n^{-\infty}$ and classical super duality, and identify $K_n^{-\infty}$ and $K_n^{+\infty}$ as Ringel duals. We also revisit mixed Schur--Weyl duality for general linear Lie superalgebras within the same framework.

papers.title: A refinement of the strange duality conjecture on K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $v,w$ be primitive Mukai vectors of positive rank on a polarized K3 surface with $\chi(v\otimes w)=0$. Marian and Oprea conjectured that the strange duality map $H^0(M(v),\Theta_w)^\vee\to H^0(M(w),\Theta_v)$ is either zero or an isomorphism. We give three families of counterexamples to this conjecture. In each of them the map is nonzero but fails to be an isomorphism: in the first (a quartic surface) it is not surjective; in the second (Picard rank one, including very general polarized K3 surfaces) the source has strictly larger dimension than the target; and in the third (an elliptic surface) source and target both have dimension six, yet the map has rank five. The three examples share a common mechanism: one of the moduli spaces carries an effective divisor of square $-2$ on which a theta line bundle has negative degree, so that this theta line bundle is not nef and has nonvanishing higher cohomology, and the theta sections produced by the strange duality map vanish to excess order along this divisor. We therefore propose a refined conjecture, in which both theta line bundles are assumed to be big and nef, for instance ample.

papers.title: A universal group with thirteen relators
papers.abstract: We construct a finitely presented group with 13 relators that contains an isomorphic copy of every finitely presented group. This improves Valiev's bound of 21 relators for universal groups. The proof combines Valiev's construction, subgroup calculations of Kegel--Li--Ren, and small-cancellation theory.

papers.title: A variation on local trilinear form
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.

papers.title: Adjoint test modules along Cohen--Macaulay morphisms
papers.abstract: We provide a transformation rule for adjoint test modules along Cohen--Macaulay maps between Cohen--Macaulay varieties that have $F$-rational geometric fibers. This is, in part, an effective version of Enescu's theorem on the ascent of $F$-rationality under local maps with $F$-rational geometric fibers.

papers.title: Algebraic loops, braids, and tropicalization
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth complex algebraic variety. We develop a tropical framework for studying algebraic loops, i.e., free homotopy classes in $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ associated with formal loops $\mathrm{Spec}\, \mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)\to Y$. When $Y$ is very affine, every formal loop determines an integral point of $\mathrm{Trop}(Y)$. For sch\"on varieties, we prove that the associated algebraic loop is determined by this tropical point together with a connected component of the corresponding initial variety. Consequently, when all initial varieties are connected, integral tropical points classify algebraic loops. We apply this theory to the case when $Y$ is a hyperplane arrangement complement. In this case, we identify the initial varieties with complements of graded arrangements and obtain explicit representatives for algebraic loops as products of relative full twists. In type $A$, these representatives recover pure algebraic braids. For root arrangements, our construction gives a tropical interpretation of the split root valuation data of Goresky, Kottwitz, and MacPherson. Finally, we prove that the cohomology of braid varieties associated with positive algebraic braids depends only on their root valuation data.

papers.title: An elliptic curve of rank $\geq 34$ and root number $-1$ over a quadratic field
papers.abstract: In this article, we find a quadratic twist over $\mathbb{Q}$ of rank $\geq 2$ (and $\geq 3$ assuming parity) of an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ of rank $\geq 32$, recently found by Elkies, Klagsbrun, and Li. We use a family of quadratic twists of rank $\geq 2$ over $\mathbb{Q}(t)$ constructed by Mestre to search for twists $E^D$ with root number $-1$, computing all root numbers without factoring the (very large) twisting parameter $D$. As a result, we exhibit an explicit integer $D$, with $411$ digits (a square times an integer with $381$ digits), such that $E^D$ has root number $-1$ and two independent rational points. In particular, the rank of $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ is at least $34$, unconditionally, and at least $35$ if we assume the Parity Conjecture.

papers.title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.

papers.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
papers.abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.

papers.title: Approximation of graded bialgebras
papers.abstract: Motivated by an equivalence of categories established by Kapranov and Schechtman, we introduce, for each non-negative integer d, the category of connected bialgebras modulo d+1. We show that these categories fit into an inverse system of categories whose inverse limit category is equivalent to the category of connected bialgebras. In addition, we extend the notion of approximation of connected bialgebras to those that are not necessarily generated in degree 1 and show that, for connected bialgebras in the category of Yetter-Drinfeld modules over a Hopf algebra, approximation is compatible with cocycle twisting.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.

papers.title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
papers.abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mari\~no and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.

papers.title: Bar cohomology of links: beyond Milnor invariants
papers.abstract: We develop bar cohomology of link complements as an invariant of links in homology spheres. In this setting, bar cohomology is a Hopf algebra which is calculable using surfaces and their intersection curves in a link complement. In this first in a sequence of works, we introduce the invariant and show that it defines a canonical subspace of the tensor Hopf algebra, which already encodes information about Milnor's link invariants and provides geometrically significant information beyond them.

papers.title: Coefficient lifting for skew divided differences and triple Schubert coefficients
papers.abstract: Skew divided difference operators \(\partial_{w/v}\), introduced by Macdonald, play an important role in the study of Schubert polynomials and their structure constants. For permutations \(u,v,w\in S_n\), we show that the coefficient of each monomial \(\xx^\alpha\) in \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\), where \(\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\) is the double Schubert polynomial, is a single triple Schubert coefficient evaluated at \(\tb=0\), whose indices form an explicit lift of \((u,v,w)\) to \(S_{n+\abs{\alpha}}\). As an application, we show that every coefficient of \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx)\) is a single Schubert structure constant. This gives a new proof of Kirillov's conjecture that these coefficients are nonnegative.

papers.title: Complete homogeneous varieties over a field
papers.abstract: The main objects of this paper are complete homogeneous varieties under the action of a semisimple group $G$ over field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. When the isotropy groups of the geometric points are smooth parabolics, these are classically known as twisted flag varieties and are well studied in the literature. If the smoothness assumption is removed, we get a larger class of varieties which we call as \emph{twisted parabolic varieties}. The main goal of this paper is to study the structure, classification and properties of these varieties. We first understand their structure over a separable closure of $k$ by classifying non-smooth parabolics containing a Borel; this builds on the recently completed classification of such parabolics over an algebraically closed field. Then, via Galois descent we get a combinatorial criterion for such a variety to descend over $k$. We compute the Picard group of twisted parabolic varieties by embedding them into products of twisted flag varieties, study their local rigidity properties and show that they are rational if they have a $k$-rational point for $p \geq 3$. When $k$ is perfect, we show many interesting properties such as existence of a universal purely inseparable cover, transitivity of $k$-rational points under $G(k)$ as well as the existence of a smooth parabolic in the stabilizer of every such point. However, these properties fail if $k$ is imperfect and we demonstrate this with illuminating examples.

papers.title: Computing the center of a fusion category
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm for explicitly computing the categorical (Drinfeld) center of a pivotal fusion category. Our approach is based on decomposing the images of simple objects under the induction functor from the category to its center. We have implemented this algorithm in a general-purpose software framework TensorCategories for tensor categories that we develop within the open-source computer algebra system OSCAR. We compute explicit models for the centers in form of the tuples $(X,\gamma)$ where $X$ is an object and $\gamma$ is a half-braiding. From these models we can compute the $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols. Using the data from the AnyonWiki, we were able to compute the center together with its $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols for all the 279 multiplicity-free fusion categories up to rank 5, and furthermore some chosen examples of rank 6, including the Haagerup subfactor (presented in a separate paper). Some of these centers yield new high-rank and not multiplicity-free examples of modular categories, e.g. rank 21 and multiplicity 2.

papers.title: Continuous representations of the meta Hahn algebra and special functions
papers.abstract: Infinite families of biorthogonal rational functions are constructed using infinite dimensional representations of the three-generated meta Hahn algebra. Continuous Hahn and continuous dual Hahn polynomials are also recovered along the way using an embedding of the Hahn algebra inside the meta Hahn. Rational functions and polynomials arise as transition coefficients between eigenvectors and generalized eigenvectors, and their algebraic properties follow naturally from the relations of the meta Hahn algebra. Finally, biorthogonality relations are established for the rational functions introduced in the paper.

papers.title: Counting rational points on non-uniruled surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ be a non-degenerate non-uniruled irreducible projective surface of degree $d$ defined over a number field $K$, and let $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)$ be the number of rational points of $X$ of height at most $B$ that do not lie on lines contained in $X$. Assuming a suitable hypothesis on the size of the rank of Abelian varieties, we show that $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,n,d,\varepsilon}B^{\frac{n+1}{n}+\varepsilon}$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, if $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^3$ is a smooth projective surface of degree $d\ge 4$ defined over a number field $K$, then $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,d,\varepsilon} B^{4/3+\varepsilon}$. This conditionally improves a bound of Salberger for $d=4$ and $d=5$. The proof, based on an argument of Heath-Brown, consists of cutting $X$ by projective hyperplanes and using a uniform version of Faltings's Theorem, due to Dimitrov, Gao, and Habegger, to bound the number of rational points on the hyperplane sections of $X$.

papers.title: Deep Learning of Topological Equivalence Classes
papers.abstract: We demonstrate an application of deep learning to the problem of identifying whether two generating vectors correspond to topologically equivalent finite group actions on Riemann surfaces, showing how architectures developed for semantic understanding have use for pure mathematical problems. In doing so we discuss how desired algebraic structure influences model design, and explore which structural properties of topological equivalence classes the model has successfully learnt.

papers.title: Deterministic Determination of Axial Constants, Sectional Regularities and Annihilator Numbers
papers.abstract:
Axial constants and sectional regularities are recently introduced
  invariants of homogeneous polynomial ideals that, like the already
  earlier introduced annihilator numbers, depend on generic choices of
  coordinates. We provide effective characterisations of the genericity
  underlying these invariants in terms of $\beta$-maximal position and
  strong stability. In particular, we show that $\beta$-maximal position
  suffices for determining generic annihilator numbers and sectional
  regularities, while its combination with strong stability yields
  corresponding results for axial constants. We also develop
  deterministic linear algebra procedures for detecting the required
  generic positions and for computing these invariants.

papers.title: Diameter-Free Pointwise Gaussian KDE in Near-Additive Query Time
papers.abstract: Wagner asked whether Gaussian kernel density estimation in $\mathbb R^d$ admits query time $\widetilde O(d+\varepsilon^{-2})$ without dependence on the diameter of the data. We answer this affirmatively for each fixed query: a randomized data structure answers a query to additive error $\varepsilon$ with probability $1-\delta$ in time $O((d+\varepsilon^{-2})\log(d+1)\log(2/\delta))$, independently of the number of data points and of their diameter. The key ingredient is a variance bound for a Fastfood-type structured Fourier block that holds uniformly in the norm of the displacement.

papers.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite group, we obtain new double affine versions of the quantum wreath Hecke algebras, and in particular of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the centre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.

papers.title: Double covers of tori for p=2 and genuine functions
papers.abstract: In his work on $L$-embeddings and double covers of tori over local fields, Kaletha associates to a maximal torus $S$ in a connected reductive group a canonical double cover $S(F)_{\pm}$ and introduces a genuine sign function $a_S$ associated to a genuine character of $S(F)_{\pm}$. We give two constructions of this genuine sign function over a non-archimedean local field, including residual characteristic $2$. The first uses rootwise lifts to the double cover; the second, in characteristic zero, uses the exponential map. Under explicit ramification conditions, both constructions yield genuine sign functions which, in odd residual characteristic, agree with his construction. We also illustrate the case of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$. A brief announcement of the first construction appears in Appendix D of that work.

papers.title: Duality Theory for Sequent Algebras
papers.abstract: Sequent algebras were introduced by D. Vakarelov \cite{VakarelovSequentALg} as a generalization of contact algebras, replacing the binary contact relation with a relation between finite sets of regions and regions. In this paper, we present sequent algebras as Boolean algebras endowed with a finitary closure operator satisfying four conditions. We study the irreducible closed sets of these operators, which coincide with Vakarelov's clans, and use them to develop a topological representation theory for sequent algebras. We introduce the categories of sequent algebras and sequent spaces and establish a dual equivalence between them, as well as a restricted dual equivalence for morphisms preserving the full Boolean structure. We also characterize sequent congruences in terms of positive filters and minimally decreasing closed subsets of the associated sequent spaces. Finally, we show that the category of sequent algebras with sequent homomorphisms is topological over the category of Boolean algebras, obtaining completeness and cocompleteness and a complete lattice structure on the sequent structures over each Boolean algebra.

papers.title: Finite Projective Source Geometry for GL2: Abel Resolvents and Central-Jet Degree Laws
papers.abstract: Starting from the two trace functions p1 = Tr(A) and p2 = Tr(A^2) for semisimple A in GL2(C), we develop the associated projective source geometry. The coordinate y = t^2/d - 1 identifies the adjoint character, and normalized Haar measure on a specified closed subgroup H of SO(3) pushes forward to a probability measure nu_H. We describe this measure through harmonic multiplicities, moments, and its Stieltjes transform, and prove that it determines H up to conjugacy within the closed-subgroup class of SO(3). A positive Abel kernel resums the projective character tower and gives a resolvent formula whose endpoint limit recovers the mass of the identity atom. We give explicit Abel transforms for the finite rotation groups and positive-dimensional benchmark sources, and derive a finite-image Frobenius-prime Abel limit from Chebotarev. For central-jet interpolation, we prove two exact degree laws: the cyclic-versus-torus minimum degree is max(n, M+1), while the normalized tetrahedral detector against S4 and A5 has minimum degree 3 for M = 1, 2 and M+2 for M >= 3. We also compute the integral image of the tetrahedral averaging functional, obtaining 2Z for every M >= 2. All results are stated with their hypotheses. The paper does not claim a general infinite-spectrum Beyond Endoscopy trace formula or transfer of central-jet vanishing to orbital kernels.

papers.title: Fppf-descent for condensed animated rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we define "animated affinoid algebras" and prove some basic properties of them. Then we generalize the result of the previous paper of the author and the result of Lucas Mann (fppf-descent for discrete rings or affinoid algebras) to discrete animated rings or animated affinoid algebras.

papers.title: Fractional DAG treewidth controls DAG treewidth: profile reorientation and VC-dimension rounding
papers.abstract: For a nonempty finite graph, let \(F\) be its fractional DAG treewidth, maximized over all acyclic orientations. Its DAG treewidth is at most \(160F^3\ln(16F)\). This answers the boundedness question of Bressan, Lanzinger, and Roth. Reorienting the graph converts shattered source profiles into projective-plane obstructions, which bound their VC dimension by \(5F^2\). Classical epsilon-net rounding then converts fractional bag covers to integral ones without changing the decomposition.

papers.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.

papers.title: Fundamental Groups and Coregularity: Klt Pairs with Trivial and Nef Log-Anticanonical Class
papers.abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we show that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ and arbitrary dimension the fundamental group $\pi_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We reduce this statement to klt Calabi-Yau pairs with standard coefficients of dimension $c$. In the cases $0\le c\le2$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. Combining the reduction with the recent regular-locus theorem of Fu-Guo-Song-Wang, we prove the coregularity bound in every dimension. In particular, for a projective klt pair $(X,D)$ with $-(K_X+D)$ nef, the orbifold fundamental group of the smooth locus is virtually abelian of rank at most $2\, {\rm dim}X$.

papers.title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
papers.abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_\delta$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_\delta$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

papers.title: Gluing weak approximability along recollements
papers.abstract: We study whether weak approximability glues along recollements of triangulated categories that are compactly generated by a single object. This is applied to derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and prescribed support for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.

papers.title: Good stratifications of non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties admit good stratifications. As an application, we study variation of the Milnor fibrations in pencils associated with non-degenerate hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: Higher Verlinde categories of reductive groups
papers.abstract: We define tensor categories ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}(G)$ in characteristic $p$ for connected reductive groups $G$ and positive integers $n$, generalising the semisimple Verlinde categories ${\sf Ver}_p(G)$ originating from Gelfand-Kazhdan and the higher Verlinde categories ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ for ${\rm SL}_2$ defined by Benson-Etingof-Ostrik. The construction is based on the definition of ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ as an abelian envelope of a quotient of a category of tilting modules, but we also introduce an expanded construction which refines the ${\rm SL}_2$ case and gives new results. In particular, the union ${\sf Ver}_{p^\infty}(G)$ can be derived from the perfection of $G$; certain exact sequences in ${\sf Rep}G$ map to exact sequences in ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}(G)$; and the underlying abelian category of ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ can be expressed as a subcategory of ${\sf Rep}{\rm SL}_2$, or as a Serre quotient of a subcategory of ${\sf Rep}{\rm SL}_2$.

papers.title: Holomorphic isomonodromic deformations of Higgs bundles: absolute lifting, spectral flatness, and nilpotent rigidity
papers.abstract: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth projective family, and fix a semisimple flat bundle on a fiber $X_0$. Its isomonodromic deformation determines a holomorphic section $\sigma_{\mathrm{dR}}:S\to M_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/S)$ of the relative de Rham moduli space. Applying the relative non-abelian Hodge correspondence fiberwise gives a section $\sigma_{\mathrm{Dol}}:S\to M_{\mathrm{Dol}}(X/S)$, whose value at each $s\in S$ is the Higgs bundle corresponding to the flat bundle $\sigma_{\mathrm{dR}}(s)$. Unlike $\sigma_{\mathrm{dR}}$, the section $\sigma_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ is in general only real analytic. We study the geometric consequences of its holomorphicity along a complex analytic subvariety. First, we prove an absolute lifting theorem: the relative isomonodromic Higgs bundle admits an absolute Higgs lift, and the fiberwise harmonic metrics can be modified to solve the Hitchin--Simpson equation on the total space. Second, we prove that the spectral one-form on every resolved irreducible component of the relative spectral scheme is Gauss--Manin flat. As an application, we prove the nilpotent rigidity conjecture of Hu--Sun--Yang--Zuo: if the initial Higgs field is nilpotent, then the Higgs field remains nilpotent along the entire holomorphic isomonodromic locus.

papers.title: Holomorphy rings and the Nullstellensatz over large fields
papers.abstract: For an infinite field $K$ and an ideal $I\subseteq K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, let $J(Z_K(I))$ be the ideal of polynomials vanishing on the $K$-rational zero locus of $I$. A Nullstellensatz over $K$ is an algebraic description of this closure operator on ideals. Hilbert's classical theorem provides such a description via the radical of $I$ over any algebraically closed field. In the present article, we introduce a unifying framework for Nullstellens\"atze over arbitrary rings using the notion of an $A$-radical, for $A$ is a subring of $K(X)$ containing $K[X]$. We show that a single canonical holomorphy ring gives a Nullstellensatz over every infinite field, recovering Hilbert's theorem when $K$ is algebraically closed. In addition, we give a new characterization of large fields (in the sense of Pop) via a particular Nullstellensatz: a perfect field is large exactly when the \emph{rational} holomorphy ring $A_n(K)$--the intersection of all $K$-rational places of residue field exactly $K$--satisfies the corresponding Nullstellensatz. Finally we study the order structure of the class of rings $A$ for which the $A$-radical gives a Nullstellensatz. We show that over non-algebraically closed fields this class has no minimal element, showing there is no optimal Nullstellensatz over such fields.

papers.title: Homological Detection by Perfectoid Algebras
papers.abstract: We first establish estimates for the projective and injective dimensions for quotients of perfectoid algebras by radical ideals. As applications, we obtain homological characterizations of modules of finite injective dimension, (big) Cohen--Macaulay modules, Gorenstein local rings, and regular local rings in mixed characteristic in terms of perfectoid algebras. These are mixed characteristic analogues of the corresponding characterizations via Frobenius morphisms in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Hypergeometric local systems and parabolic bundles
papers.abstract: Beukers and Heckman gave necessary and sufficient conditions for a hypergeometric function $_n F_{n-1}$ to be algebraic. We give a new proof of this theorem by passing through the Mehta-Seshadri correspondence. In particular, we explicitly write down the parabolic bundle corresponding to a unitary hypergeometric local system.

papers.title: Hyperplane arrangements with non-formal Milnor fibers
papers.abstract: Each complex hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ gives rise to a Milnor fibration of its complement. Building on work of Zuber, we give a combinatorial sufficient condition for the Milnor fiber $F(\mathcal{A})$ to be non-$1$-formal, expressed in terms of the multinet structure on $\mathcal{A}$, and use it to produce an infinite family of monomial arrangements $\mathcal{A}(3k,3k,3)$ with non-formal Milnor fibers. We also review the relevant background on cohomology jump loci, formality, and the topology of Milnor fibers of arrangements.

papers.title: Inherent Trade-offs when Enforcing Correct Data Symmetries in Multi-head Self-attention
papers.abstract: We give a complete characterization of equivariant multi-head self-attention (MHSA): if an MHSA layer is equivariant to a symmetry group $G$, then $G$ can only act by permuting head-clusters, with QK and OV matrices satisfying an equivariance constraint tied to the group action. As a consequence, we prove that any fixed MHSA architecture that achieves exact equivariance by polynomially parameterizing unconstrained MHSA parameters inevitably leads to expressivity loss within the class of equivariant maps: the equivariance locus of unconstrained MHSA forms a union of extremely many Zariski-irreducible components in a reduced parameter space, and any single architecture covers at most one. For $G=D_4$ acting on $C$ copies of the regular representation as the token feature space, we show that there are $\Omega(C^{64})$ components for eight attention heads. We illustrate this with experiments on artificial tasks and show that the predicted head-cluster structures can arise naturally when the attention layer is pressured to become equivariant.

papers.title: Inner Products and Banach Algebra structures on Bicomplex Numbers and Their Associated Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce various types of inner products and norms on the bicomplex number system $\mathbb{C}_2$, the bicomplex vector space ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$, the space of bicomplex matrices ${C_2}^{m \times n}$, and the space of bicomplex polynomials $\mathbb{C}_2[\xi]_n$. We investigate the relationships among these inner products and norms, and establish several results. Furthermore, we prove that $\mathbb{C}_2$ and ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$ are Banach algebras and Hilbert spaces. These results provide a unified framework for the study of inner product structures and normed linear spaces over bicomplex numbers and their associated spaces.

papers.title: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
papers.abstract: We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.

papers.title: Kernels of Arithmetic Jet Spaces and Frobenius Morphism
papers.abstract:
For any $\pi$-formal group scheme $G$, the Frobenius morphism between arithmetic jet spaces restricts to generalized kernels of the projection map. Using the functorial properties of such kernels of arithmetic jet spaces, we show that this morphism is indeed induced by a natural ring map between shifted $\pi$-typical Witt vectors.
  In the special case when $G = \hat{\mathbb{G}}_a$, the arithmetic jet space, as well as the generalized kernels are affine $\pi$-formal planes with Witt vector addition as the group law. In that case the above morphism is the multiplication by $\pi$ map on Witt vector schemes. In fact, the system of arithmetic jet spaces and generalized kernels of any $\pi$-formal group scheme $G$ along with their maps and identitites satisfied among them are a generalization of the case of the Witt vector scheme with the system of maps such as the Frobenius, Verschiebung and multiplication by $\pi$.

papers.title: Left properness of Moore flows
papers.abstract: We introduce reparametrization categories with cuts. For every such category $\mathcal{P}$, the tensor product of two objectwise weak homotopy equivalences of $\mathcal{P}$-spaces is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence, and the q-model structure on $\mathcal{P}$-flows is left proper. The reparametrization categories $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{M}$, as well as the terminal category $\mathbf{1}$, have cuts. The terminal category recovers the left properness of the q-model structure on ordinary flows. We also give a symmetric reparametrization category with cuts and a strict unit. This category is not equivalent to $\mathbf{1}$.

papers.title: Limits of Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds and Moduli Spaces of Sheaves on K3 Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a compact strongly Gauduchon manifold which is a limit of compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds is bimeromorphic to a compact hyperk\"ahler manifold. This settles a case of a conjecture of Soldatenkov and Verbitsky. A closed completion of a Gauduchon metric bounds the Dirichlet energies of nearby biholomorphisms. This bound yields a meromorphic limit map, which has degree one and is therefore a bimeromorphism onto a compact hyperk\"ahler manifold. We apply this result to moduli spaces of stable torsion-free coherent sheaves on K3 surfaces. A Bott--Chern diagonal formula gives the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma, and positivity of determinant classes gives K\"ahlerness, proving Perego's conjecture.

papers.title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree
papers.abstract: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles. By settling these conjectures, we prove that a neural network with a general polynomial activation function of sufficiently large degree is identifiable.

papers.title: Linear Trace-Deficit Decay for Permanents of Positive Semidefinite Contractions
papers.abstract: Every Hermitian positive semidefinite contraction \(A\) satisfies \(\operatorname{per}(A)\leq\exp(-\operatorname{tr}(I-A)/68)\). This proves the linear trace-deficit bound conjectured by Ebrahimnejad, Nagda, and Oveis Gharan, whose estimate had quadratic dependence on the normalized deficit. The proof combines a size-biased complex Gaussian representation, a block version of Hanson–Wright decoupling, and a rational Loewner majorant. The constant is uniform in the dimension and is not optimized.

papers.title: Local stability of Frobenius and Artin--Schreier base-change: a comparison
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\Delta)\to C$ be a family of pairs over a smooth curve in positive characteristic $p>0$. We study the discrepancies of divisors over the base-change $(X,\Delta)\to C$ along Artin--Schreier and Frobenius covers of $C$, through ramification data for Artin--Schreier and degree $p$ purely inseparable extensions of DVRs. As an application, we recover a result of Hu and Zong about permanence of local stability for such base-change.

papers.title: Matrix Completion Discriminants
papers.abstract: We introduce the matrix completion discriminant of a graph as the Zariski closure of the set of partial symmetric matrices whose completion fibers fail to meet a rank stratum transversely. A clique-sum formula for the matrix completion discriminant is established for arbitrary graphs, while explicit defining equations for cycles are obtained in terms of iterated resultants. Using these results together with the analysis of $K_4$-minor-free graphs, we prove that for every cycle-completable graph, the discriminant factors into determinant factors from maximal cliques and resultant factors from chordless cycles.

papers.title: Minimal energy local systems on curves
papers.abstract:
Let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ be an orientable topological surface of genus $g$ with $n$ punctures. When $g = 0$, Deroin and Tholozan studied the class of supra-maximal representations $\pi_1(\Sigma_{0,n})\to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, and they showed that the supra-maximal representations form a compact component of a real relative character variety. We study a collection of rank $r$ local systems on $\Sigma_{g,n}$ which we call of minimal energy. These are generalizations of supra-maximal representations, and underlie polarizable complex variations of Hodge structure for any choice of complex structure on $\Sigma_{g,n}$. Like the supra-maximal representations, the minimal energy local systems form compact components of relative character varieties of real forms of $\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb{C})$.
  We show that when the local monodromy data around the punctures is chosen to be unitary and generic, and the relative character variety is nonempty, these minimal energy local systems always exist. When $g > 0$, we show that the minimal energy local systems come from unitary representations of $\pi_1(\Sigma_{g,n})$. If $g = 0$ we show that they do not always come from unitary representations, and we study their structure in general.

papers.title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

papers.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.

papers.title: Nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth curves and arbitrarily negative Wahl defects
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth projective curves of genus at least two, constructed by gluing products of open subsets of a curve with a disc using nonlinear changes of the disc coordinate. Their zero sections have normal bundles of negative degree and contract to normal surface singularities. For the minimal good resolution \((X,E) \to (V,0)\) of a normal complex surface singularity other than a rational double point, the Wahl defect is defined by \(\Delta(V,0) := h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2S_X)\), where \(E\) is reduced and \(S_X = \Theta_X(-\log E)\). We give a finite formula for this defect in terms of extension obstructions when \(E\) is a single smooth curve. For our constructed neighborhoods, the formula involves extensions of functions alone, includes obstructions at every order, and gives a sharp lower bound depending only on the genus. We apply the theory to hyperelliptic curves and smooth plane curves. Both families consist of singularities that are neither \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein nor quasi-homogeneous. The hyperelliptic examples realize every nonpositive integer as a Wahl defect and attain the genus bound in every genus at least two. They disprove Wahl's Main Conjecture, which asserts nonnegativity for non-Gorenstein singularities, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case.

papers.title: Normal complex surface singularities with rational homology disk smoothings
papers.abstract: We prove that a normal surface singularity whose minimal good resolution graph has at least two nodes does not admit a rational homology disk smoothing. Together with the earlier graph classifications and the analytic classifications of Fowler and Wahl, this gives a complete classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings and proves Wahl's conjecture. The same argument also proves Wahl's Rational Conjecture.

papers.title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
papers.abstract: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^{\nu}_{\lambda,\mu}=3$, then $c^{M\nu}_{M\lambda,M\mu}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{\lambda,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $\beta=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $\sigma$, we show that if $\beta$ is $\sigma$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $\sigma$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $\sigma$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.

papers.title: On constructibility of klt type varieties and simple $D$-module
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the combination of dense klt type and $\mathcal{D}$-simplicity property establishes the klt type property.

papers.title: On higher Pythagoras numbers of real polynomial rings
papers.abstract: We show that the higher Pythagoras numbers for the polynomial ring are infinite $p_{2s}(K[x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n])=\infty$ provided that $K$ is a formally real field, $n\geq2$ and $s\geq 1$. This almost fully solves an old question \cite[Problem 8]{cldr1982}. The remaining open cases are precisely $n=1$ and $s>1$. Moreover, we study in detail the cone of binary octics that are sums of fourth powers of quadratic forms. We determine its facial structure as well as its algebraic boundary. This can also be seen as sums of fourth powers of linear forms on the second Veronese of $\mathbb{P}^1$. As a result, we disprove a conjecture of Reznick \cite[Conjecture 7.1]{reznick2011} which states that if a binary form $f$ is a sum of fourth powers, then it can be written as $f=f_1^2+f_2^2$ for some nonnegative forms $f_1,f_2$.

papers.title: On partial representations of pointed Hopf algebras
papers.abstract: The theory of partial representations first appeared in the context of groups to deal with restrictions of representations to non-invariant subspaces. Partial representations of a group $G$ correspond to representations of a groupoid algebra constructed out of $G$. The notion of a partial representation can be extended to the context of Hopf algebras. For a Hopf algebra $H$, its partial representations correspond to representations of a Hopf algebroid $H_{par}$, also constructed out of data coming from $H$. In this work, we describe the structure of the algebra $H_{par}$ for $H$ being a pointed Hopf algebra with a finite group of grouplikes $G(H)$. This algebra can be explicitly written as a direct sum, reflecting the groupoid algebra associated to the group $G(H)$. Explicit examples of rank one Hopf algebras are done in the nilpotent and the non-nilpotent cases.

papers.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
papers.abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

papers.title: On the fundamental groups of subelliptic varieties
papers.abstract: We show that the fundamental group of any smooth subelliptic variety is finite. Moreover, it is also proved that every finite group can be realized as the fundamental group of a smooth subelliptic variety. As a consequence, it follows that there exists a smooth subelliptic variety homotopy equivalent to the $n$-sphere if and only if $n>1$. This result can be considered as a negative answer to the algebraic version of Gromov's problem on the homotopy types of Oka manifolds.

papers.title: On the identifiability and semi-algebraicity of ReLU neuromanifolds
papers.abstract: We study several aspects of the semi-algebraicity of the neuromanifold $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbf{d}}$ of a feedforward ReLU neural network. We prove that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbf{d}}$ in general is not a semi-algebraic quotient of the space of parameters of the network, but it can be approximated (in a precise sense) by semi-algebraic spaces. We then consider the notion of identifiable subsets of the space of parameters, where the network does not have any hidden symmetries. We prove that the maximal identifiable subset is semi-algebraic for any neural network with semi-algebraic activation functions. Lastly, we compute explicitly the identifiable subset of a shallow ReLU network and prove that for input dimensions $\ge 3$ and width $\ge 6$ it is not euclidean open.

papers.title: On the variety of sum of powers of certain complete intersection forms
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a homogeneous polynomial (form). If the annihilator ideal $F^\perp$ is a complete intersection, then $F$ is called as a complete intersection form. For many complete intersection forms, we show that its minimal apolar ideal is a complete intersection and further we show that ${\rm VSP}(F)$ is irreducible and compute its dimension.

papers.title: Orthogonal circles and a fixed-dimensional separated-distance counterexample
papers.abstract: A finite set of points in Euclidean space is distance-separated if the lengths of any two different unordered edges differ by at least one. Counting distances shows that an n-point distance-separated set has diameter at least binom(n,2), approximately n^2/2, and Erdős asked whether the diameter must be at least (1-o(1))n^2. Ho showed that the answer is no if the dimension may grow with n. The first version of this paper gave counterexamples with diameter below 0.74n^2 in a single fixed dimension. We give a sharper explicit fixed-dimensional counterexample: for every integer n at least 36354, there is a distance-separated n-point set in R^81794 with diameter strictly below (147/200)n^2 = 0.735n^2. The finite conclusion has an accompanying Lean 4 proof, including minimum distance at least one for distinct points and the actual set diameter bound. As in the first version, this construction replaces each vertex of a large macro simplex by a cluster of points. A standard Gram-deficit completion arranges those clusters on circles in mutually orthogonal planes. The arrangement makes every distance between two clusters an exact, explicit, increasing function of two digits and reduces the number of coordinates from 9m-1 to 3m-1 for m clusters. A single quadratic-residue ruler controls both the distances inside clusters and the digits between them. The proof is self-contained apart from Bertrand's postulate.

papers.title: Perfectoid Pure and Signature Pairs
papers.abstract: We extend perfectoid purity and related invariants to divisor pairs in mixed characteristic. The resulting purity condition agrees with $F$-purity of pairs in characteristic $p$ as defined by Hara--Watanabe. For normal (respectively, demi-normal) log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs, we show that perfectoid pure implies log canonical (respectively, semi-log canonical). We similarly establish adjunction for perfectoid pure pairs and inversion of adjunction for principal pairs in complete intersections along a Cartier divisor. We also define perfectoid pure thresholds and prove localization and base change results, including a formula for local extensions with regular closed fiber. We establish upper bounds in terms of analytic spread, dimension, and log canonical thresholds. Finally, we also introduce perfectoid signatures for divisor pairs in mixed characteristic whose positivity characterizes the BCM-regularity of log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs. We prove a transformation rule under finite extensions and show continuity and convexity for scalings of a Cartier divisor.

papers.title: Polygraphic resolutions for operated algebras
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the structure of operated polygraphs as a categorical model for rewriting in operated algebras, generalizing Gr\"obner--Shirshov bases with non-monomial termination orders. We show how to construct polygraphic resolutions of free operated algebras from confluent and terminating presentations. We provide a combinatorial description of critical branchings of operated polygraphs using the structure of polyautomata introduced in this paper. Polyautomata are linear polygraphs equipped with an operator structure formalized by a pushdown automaton. Finally, we apply our constructions to several families of operated algebras, including Rota--Baxter algebras, differential algebras, and differential Rota--Baxter algebras.

papers.title: Positivity of Wahl defects and representations from index-one covers
papers.abstract: Let \((X,E) \to (V,0)\) be the minimal good resolution of a normal complex surface singularity, with \(E\) reduced. The Wahl defect is \(\Delta(V,0) :=h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2 S_X)\), where \(S_X=\Theta_X(-\log E)\). For non-Gorenstein \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein singularities \((V,0)\), we prove that \(\Delta(V,0)\geq0\), with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case. This proves Wahl's Main Conjecture in this class and his \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein and Rational Conjectures. The proof expresses \(\Delta\) as the multiplicity of the canonical character in a representation constructed from differential forms and residues. We also prove \(\Delta+4p_g\geq0\) for arbitrary normal surface singularities, with equality precisely for rational quasi-homogeneous singularities. For smoothings of rational surface singularities, we give a Riemann--Roch formula for the lengths of the cokernels of the restriction maps to the central fiber for all reflexive canonical powers, in terms of the Milnor number and periodic local Riemann--Roch corrections. This yields numerical and representation-theoretic criteria for \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein smoothings, defined as quotients of equivariant smoothings of the index-one cover with trivial group action on the base. If a rational singularity admits a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein smoothing, such smoothings are precisely those with minimal Milnor number, or equivalently those whose smoothing components have minimal dimension. Combining these results, we prove that every rational homology disk smoothing is \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein, has a rational weighted homogeneous central fiber, and occurs over a one-dimensional smoothing component. Together with the known weighted homogeneous classification, this completes the analytic classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings.

papers.title: Quantized integral models of reductive monoids
papers.abstract: We construct quantized integral models of reductive monoids and establish their finite-generation properties. We also describe the quantized coordinate rings of the basic affine spaces explicitly in terms of Lusztig's dual canonical bases. The results will be used in the companion paper \cite{CJ2} to establish a classification theorem for split reductive monoids over arbitrary connected base schemes.

papers.title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
papers.abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively \'etale and quasi-\'etale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-\'Alvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissi\`ere, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an \'etale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.

papers.title: Rational Fourth Powers Summing to 82
papers.abstract: We prove that the only primitive positive integer solutions of $x^4+y^4=82z^4$ are $(1,3,1)$ and $(3,1,1)$. An arithmetic reduction lifts every other putative solution to an elliptic curve over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{41},\sqrt{2})$. An explicit 2-descent determines its rank as 3. A logarithmic functional then excludes all nonzero parameters in the relevant 2-adic disc, including both relative sign patterns at the two places above 2. The same argument determines every point of the auxiliary quartic whose parameter is rational: only the two points at infinity occur. Exact square identities also determine the quotient modulo 2, prove that the displayed subgroup has odd index, and give the vanishing of the 2-primary part of the Tate–Shafarevich group. Two reductions determine the torsion. The finite arithmetic certificates are supplied in two self-contained Python programs; no height cutoff or conjectural rank computation is used.

papers.title: Rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ when $N$ is non-squarefree
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be a positive integer and $X_0(N)^*$ be the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(N)$ by its full group of Atkin-Lehner involutions. Elkies conjectures that the rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ are only cusps or CM points when $N$ is large enough. We establish an integrality result for the $j$-invariants of non-cuspidal rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ when $N$ is non-squarefree, representing a significant step toward resolving a key subcase of Elkies' conjecture. To this end, we prove the existence of rank-zero quotients of certain modular Jacobians $J_0(pq)$. Furthermore, in the non-squarefree case we provide a complete classification of the rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ of genus $1 \leq g \leq 5$, when they are finite. In the process we identify exceptional rational points on $X_0(75)^*$ and $X_0(147)^*$ which were not known before.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional vector bundle
papers.abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles and let $V_X$ and $V_Y$ be exceptional vector bundles on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $V_X^\perp\simeq V_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.

papers.title: Rectangular Symmetry for Catalan Functions
papers.abstract: Katabolizable tableaux provide a combinatorial formula for the Schur coefficients of Catalan functions. We prove that a tableau involution preserves katabolizability under antidiagonal reflection of any upper root ideal. This involution complements shape and content in a fixed rectangle and preserves charge. We obtain a bijective proof of the rectangular symmetry of these coefficients.

papers.title: Robustness of quantum spectrum estimation: weak Schur sampling under noisy inputs
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of weak Schur sampling (WSS) under noisy inputs. Many optimal quantum learning algorithms rely on this measurement, for instance in quantum spectrum estimation (QSE) and quantum state tomography (QST).
