The standard analysis of WSS, QSE and QST assumes that the $n$ input copies of the target state $\rho$ are identical, i.e. $\rho^{\otimes n}$. We study what happens when they are not, a more realistic noisy scenario that breaks the very permutation symmetry on which WSS is built. In the simplest model the input is a noisy product state: the copies are independent but not necessarily identical and each is $\epsilon$-close in trace distance to the $d$-dimensional target state $\rho$. A naive argument via the data-processing inequality allows the per-copy errors to accumulate to $n\epsilon$ on the measurement outcome. We show that for QSE via WSS this does not happen: the expected estimation error in total variation is at most $\epsilon+\eta(n,d)$, where $\eta(n,d)=O(d/\sqrt n)$ is the noiseless error, and the additive noise term $\epsilon$ is optimal. The output error does not grow with $n$ even though the input error does; in this sense WSS is robust. Beyond noisy product states, for arbitrary input $\omega$ we show that the error is at most $\eta(n,d)+\frac{1}{n}\|\omega-\rho^{\otimes n}\|_{W_1}$, where $W_1$ is the quantum Wasserstein distance of De Palma et al. In particular, our results imply, for the first time, noise-robustness of Keyl and Werner's seminal algorithm for QSE, more than two decades after its introduction. Finally, we show that the noise cannot be too bad: within our model of robustness the promise on the input cannot be weakened to closeness of single-copy marginals or to a global trace-distance budget alone, as in both cases some inputs defeat every measurement and estimator.

papers.title: Saturated directed spaces and generalized clocks
papers.abstract: We construct a Hausdorff saturated directed space whose directed path space between two distinct points has nontrivial fundamental group although the corresponding trace space is a square. A clock is a directed space with submetrizable underlying space; a timed space is a saturated directed space equipped with a regular directed map to a clock. Over every fixed clock, timed spaces form a locally presentable category, and their quotients from paths to traces are trivial Hurewicz fibrations with continuous sections. For Hausdorff saturated directed spaces whose compact subspaces are metrizable, these quotients are trivial q-fibrations. We construct a globular clock containing the directed circle and admitting regular maps from all q-cofibrant globular realizations, whereas a finite cellular example admits no regular map to the circle. Normalization also gives a proof of the quotient theorem for execution paths and establishes the homotopy lifting property for nondecreasing reparametrizations.

papers.title: Series of Fano quiver moduli from extended Dynkin quivers
papers.abstract: Associated to small extended Dynkin quivers, we construct series of Fano varieties of fixed Picard rank at most five and arbitrary even dimension, which admit a very explicit description of their geometry. For example, they all admit a flat morphism to a projective space, whose general fiber is a product of projective lines. We also give a closed formula for all Betti numbers, and interpret this formula in terms of an action of a cohomological Hall algebra on the cohomology of all the varieties in a series.

papers.title: Sharp fractional Helly bounds for common affine flats
papers.abstract: If an $\alpha$ fraction of the $(d-k+1)$-tuples of closed convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ have an intersection containing a whole affine $k$-flat, then a fraction $1-(1-\alpha)^{1/(d-k+1)}$ of the sets share such a flat. This coefficient is best possible, resolving the sharp fractional De Santis question of Ludwigson and Soberón. The geometric result behind the bound is $(d-k)$-collapsibility of the common-flat complex, proved by coordinating convex sweeps in varying quotient spaces.

papers.title: Stable algebraic families of polarized dynamical systems and exceptional extensions
papers.abstract: The notion of exceptional maps in arbitrary dimension was recently introduced by Ji, Song, and Xie. In this paper, we introduce exceptional extensions of polarized dynamical systems: a family of systems admitting a positive-dimensional exceptional factor whose generic fiber dynamics have simultaneous local product coordinates with an isotrivial system. We then prove that an algebraic family of polarized endomorphisms of normal projective varieties over a quasi-projective curve is $J$-stable on a nonempty Zariski open subset if and only if it is isotrivial or it is an exceptional extension after a finite base change. This extends McMullen's theorem for stable algebraic families of rational maps to higher dimension. One ingredient is inspired by Ji and Xie's proof of McMullen's theorem: the use of homoclinic orbits and the multipliers of adjoint periodic points to control local return maps. The new ingredients are a higher-dimensional algebraization method and an inductive rigidity argument for the fiber dynamics, which together yield the exceptional extension structure.

papers.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
papers.abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

papers.title: Subset Sum in time O(2^{0.4877n})
papers.abstract: We present a uniform randomized classical algorithm for Subset Sum with running time O(2^{0.4877n}) in the word-RAM model, for inputs whose integer bit lengths are polynomially bounded in the number n of input integers. The algorithm halts on every execution and answers correctly with probability at least 2/3. The construction builds on OpenAI’s “Subset Sum in Time O(2^{0.49n})” (4 October 2026), retaining its framework of isolation, a capped preliminary search, a modular checksum, and alias subtraction. Two components are replaced: an alias procedure that computes phase sums using a smaller modulus, and a family of 43 checksum filters selected according to the input pattern. The analysis combines an averaged small-layer lemma, grouping by reduced and unreduced subset sums, and rigorous numerical certificates. Verification scripts using Arb ball arithmetic check the alias constraints and 430 moment inequalities. The argument relies on results from the earlier paper, which are restated in an appendix; the numerical certificates verify specified inequalities rather than formally verifying the entire proof.

papers.title: Tensor-generating line bundles on toric varieties
papers.abstract: A line bundle is $\otimes$-generating if its powers generate the derived category of perfect complexes. Refining the derived Nakai--Moishezon criterion of Ito--Olander, we characterize $\otimes$-generating line bundles on proper toric varieties by a combinatorial criterion on the fan, leading to the notion of $\otimes$-generating fans characterizing $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Furthermore, we prove an analogue of Kleiman's criterion of ampleness for $\otimes$-generation. As applications, we provide several examples including: (i) smooth proper fourfolds with no $\otimes$-generating line bundle, by showing that products of two or more positive-dimensional proper toric varieties admit a $\otimes$-generating line bundle only when they are projective, (ii) families of smooth non-projective proper threefolds with $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Finally, we study subvarieties obstructing $\otimes$-generation of canonical bundles and implications to autoequivalences of derived categories.

papers.title: The chain replacement of a poset flow
papers.abstract: We introduce the chain replacement of a poset flow: it is obtained by considering the simplicial nerves of the posets of strictly increasing chains in the given poset, ordered by refinement. It maps posets to q-cofibrant flows and inclusions of posets to q-cofibrations. Using the combinatorial properties of the chain replacement, we prove that pushouts along the chain replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets induce trivial h-cofibrations on spaces of execution paths between states of the original flow. By introducing the Hurewicz model structure on flows (or H-model structure), we deduce the same property for any q-cofibrant replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets.

papers.title: The Coloured Sand Theorem: the p-part of the sandpile group of the Hamming graph, for every prime p dividing q and every dimension d
papers.abstract: Let $H(d,q)=K_q^{d}$ be the Hamming graph and $K(H(d,q))$ its sandpile group (critical group, Jacobian). For primes $p\nmid q$ its $p$-part was determined by Jacobson, Niedermaier and Reiner in 2003, who wrote that the other primes appear "to be difficult, due to bad behavior of its $p$-primary structure". We determine the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $K(H(d,q))$ for every prime $p$ dividing $q$ and every $d$, by an explicit rule. After the splitting of Jacobson, Niedermaier and Reiner, the group is a sum of cokernels of operators $q(c+H)+U$ on the Boolean lattice (Theorem A). These split over the indecomposable tilting modules $T(\lambda)$ of $SL_2$ in characteristic $p$ that occur in a tensor power of the natural module. The contribution of $T(\lambda)$ consists of explicit small cyclic factors and of $2^{|I|}$ large ones, where $I$ is the set of positions of the nonzero base-$p$ digits of $\lambda+1$ below the leading one. The large ones are obtained by pooling explicit integers, built from binomial valuations and base-$p$ carries, into a non-increasing sequence (Theorems I and J). The proof writes down explicit $\mathbb{Z}_p$-lattices for all tilting modules of $SL_2$, one move per base-$p$ digit; it reduces each contribution to the Smith form of an explicit $2^{|I|}\times2^{|I|}$ matrix, and computes that form as in our proof for the hypercube (The Dancing Sand Theorem), the case $p=2$. We also give closed formulas that need no pooling: for $p>d$ with ballot numbers (B), for the exponent with every prime (C), and for the number of cyclic factors (D). This proves Conjecture I of version 3 of this paper. Every result of the paper, Theorems A–J, is checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib, for every prime, and the Lean project was rebuilt from its sources on GitHub's machines, on Mathlib's published build. This work has not been refereed by a human expert.

papers.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
papers.abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

papers.title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
papers.abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: The monodromy conjecture for high order poles, and norms of residue antiderivatives
papers.abstract: We prove the strong local monodromy conjecture for poles of order at least $n-1$ of the naive motivic zeta-function for a complex polynomial of $n$ variables. Moreover, for every such pole $s$, we construct an explicit homology $\exp(2\pi i s)$-eigencycle in a neighborhood of any given 1-dimensional exceptional stratum contributing the pole. The proof combines topological techniques developed by the author with a fact of birational geometry discovered by AI.

papers.title: The P\'olya--Vinogradov inequality with $\log\log q$
papers.abstract: We prove unconditionally that every primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q\ge3$ has character sums of size at most $C\sqrt q\log\log q$. Montgomery and Vaughan proved this bound under the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and Paley showed that it is optimal. The proof uses the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$, which also gives $|L'/L(1,\chi)|\ll\log\log q$ and two-sided bounds for the Euler--Kronecker constants of the cyclotomic fields $\mathbb Q(\zeta_q)$.

papers.title: The rank-one Dixmier conjecture for elements of mass at most six
papers.abstract: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let P,Q in A_1(K) satisfy [Q,P]=1. We prove that P,Q generate A_1(K) if either has mass at most six, meaning at most six nonzero homogeneous components for the grading deg X=1, deg Y=-1, with no degree bound on either element. This extends the four-component theorem of Guccione, Guccione and Valqui. The proof combines their Newton-polygon restrictions with a classification of polynomial pairs r,f satisfying an associated scalar differential equation under the condition that r^2 has at most six monomial terms. The scalar argument uses a two-dimensional Vandermonde kernel, Rolle's theorem, and a sign and parity obstruction. The scalar classification and the mass bound reduce the crossing cases to a binomial-power face. We exclude that face using at most one Newton cut, without a mass bound on the transformed pair. We also exclude a family of pure-power crossing faces with prime outer exponent, without a mass bound. A seven-term scalar solution shows that the scalar classification is sharp, although its associated Weyl face is excluded by the pure-power theorem. Theorem 1.1 is formalized in Lean 4 and registered as Palomar entry PALOMAR-2026-10-05-000006, version 2.

papers.title: The Richelot isogeny graph and paramodular forms of weight 3: Atkin-Lehner signs and certified spectra
papers.abstract: The Richelot $(2,2)$-isogeny graph $G_p$ of superspecial abelian surfaces in characteristic $p$ is the genus-2 analogue of the supersingular isogeny graph: its weighted adjacency matrix is a Brandt matrix for a compact inner form of $\mathrm{GSp}_4$, and it commutes with an Atkin-Lehner involution $R(\pi)$. Refining Ibukiyama's conjectures, we conjecture the automorphic origin and the $R(\pi)$-sign of every eigenvalue: Eisenstein, Saito-Kurokawa, Yoshida and paramodular eigenvalues, and pairs of type-Va eigensystems that only $R(\pi)$ separates. We compute $G_p$ at 33 primes, with up to 2176 vertices, and certify the predicted eigenvalues and signs in exact arithmetic; at $p=167$ and $173$, where the sign prediction first becomes non-trivial, the graph carries the predicted eigenvalue $-8$ with sign $-1$. For every prime we prove that each type-Va parameter contributes exactly one eigenline of each $R(\pi)$-sign, a closed formula for the trace of $R(\pi)$, and a Fricke sign bias. If no further CAP representations occur, the non-trivial spectrum lies in $[-8\sqrt{2}, 6+4\sqrt{2}]$, both ends being sharp under the conjecture, and only Saito-Kurokawa eigenvalues exceed $8\sqrt{2}$; at all 104 primes $p\le 601$ the extreme eigenvalue computed by Florit and Smith agrees with the largest Saito-Kurokawa one. Finally, the irrational roots of the residual square factor form one Galois orbit with full symmetric Galois group at each certified prime $p\ge 29$, and the spectrum appears to follow a Plancherel law.

papers.title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.

papers.title: The Willow Transform and the Blind Zone Theorem: A Sharp Information-Theoretic Obstruction in the Turán Hierarchy for the Riemann xi-Function
papers.abstract: Let Xi(t) = xi(1/2 + it) be the Riemann Xi-function, let Xi(t) = sum_{k>=0} (-1)^k c_k t^{2k} be its even Taylor expansion at the origin, and let D(n,r) = det[c_{n+i-j}] (i,j = 0..r-1) be the Toeplitz minors whose positivity for all n >= 0, r >= 1 is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (RH). We prove a sharp and quantitative obstruction in the resulting hierarchy of criteria. Parametrising the zeros of G(z) = sum c_k z^k by beta_j = -1/z_j, we establish by the dual Jacobi-Trudi identity the exact identity D(n,r) = s_{(r^n)}(beta), the Schur function of the rectangular partition (r^n) in the variables beta. A zero of zeta off the critical line contributes to beta a conjugate pair rho e^{+-i theta} whose angle theta is exactly the vertical angle of the violating pair of zeros, while zeros on the critical line contribute positive real variables. For two variables we prove the closed form s_{(a,b)}(rho e^{i theta}, rho e^{-i theta}) = rho^{a+b} sin((a+1-b) theta) / sin theta = rho^{a+b} U_{a-b}(cos theta), U_k being the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, so that the sign is governed by the classical criterion U_k(cos theta) > 0 if and only if (k+1) theta < pi. Since a Schur function in two variables can be expanded through the coproduct s_lambda(X sqcup Y) = sum_mu s_mu(X) s_{lambda/mu}(Y), and since s_mu(X) > 0 for positive real X, positivity reduces to the two-variable factors, whose index k = a - b is bounded by the number of columns r, not by the shift n. This yields: Blind Zone Theorem. If a violating pair subtends a vertical angle theta < pi/(r+1), then every Toeplitz minor D(n,r') with r' <= r is strictly positive, notwithstanding the presence of non-real zeros. The critical strip together with gamma_1 = 14.134725141... forces theta <= theta_max = 2 arctan(1/(2 gamma_1)) = 0.07071826... rad, whence pi/theta_max = 44.424... and therefore every order r <= 43 is completely non-discriminating. We emphasise that the exponential bound is on the order r and not on the shift n; we exhibit the mechanism and show the contrary n-based bound is false. We also record the refutation of a "universal covering law" previously conjectured by the author, and a floating-point artefact that nearly produced a false refutation of the main theorem. No claim of a proof of RH is made.

papers.title: Topological Hochschild homology of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra II
papers.abstract: We compute topological Hochschild homology of $\mathbb{E}_3$-MU-algebra forms of the second truncated Brown-Peterson spectrum with Adams summand coefficients at $p=2$ and conditionally at arbitrary primes. We also provide a new computational tool, a variant of the Brun spectral sequence, for computing topological Hochschild homology of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra with certain coefficients. As a consequence, we show that $\mathbb{E}_3$-MU-algebra forms of truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n\rangle$ are not Thom spectra at the prime $p=2$ for any $n\ge 2$.

papers.title: Two-step nilpotent monodromy of local systems on special varieties
papers.abstract: We address a question of Campana by giving a criterion for when nilpotent local systems on quasi-projective varieties have 2-step nilpotent monodromy. As an application, we prove that the monodromy group of any complex local system on smooth complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana or $h$-special (e.g. containg a Zariski dense entire curve), is virtually 2-step nilpotent. This result sharply refines a theorem of Cadorel, Yamanoi, and the second author. To establish this result, we develop a deformation theory for certain local systems on quasi-compact K\"ahler manifolds by constructing universal deformations for such local systems.

papers.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.

papers.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.

papers.title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
papers.abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.
